title: Rudolf Blaschka 1892 sketchbook working-note and surrogate-delivery audit — pass 03
scope: Backend-only refinement of sketchbook pages 26-28 and digital-surrogate integrity. This file supersedes the provisional p26-p28 readings in the earlier crosswalk where they differ.
frontend_policy: Do not expose sketchbook images, thumbnails, page-derived geometries, or these working-note inferences on public GitHub Pages in this phase.

supersedes.reason: higher-resolution visual reading plus external historical controls

reading_confidence.Lange_Brinckmann: medium-high; Rudolf appears to reverse the historically attested firm-name order Brinckmann & Lange
reading_confidence.Obere_Strasse: medium; likely shorthand/variant for Obernstraße in the context of the following corner reference

external_controls.business: metalware factory; originated in Christian Baldewein's tinsmithing business
external_controls.source: Weser-Kurier regional-history article on Am Wall 165
external_controls.evidential_role: strong identity/location control; does not prove what Rudolf purchased or why he noted the firm

external_controls.business: gold- and silverware / jeweler with workshop and retail business
external_controls.source: Bremen monument/history material and family/company chronicle
external_controls.evidential_role: strong corner-location control; the firm name Brinckmann & Lange was adopted in 1891
period directory control; contains resident, street, commercial and trade sections. Exact Schüsselkorb 14 occupant still to be extracted.

spatial_sequence.working_hypothesis: The lines form a spatially coherent Bremen Altstadt sequence rather than unrelated later notes: Am Wall -> Schüsselkorb -> Sögestraße/Obernstraße -> Markt.
spatial_sequence.guard: Distances are modern geometric controls, not reconstructed 1892 walking distances.

itinerary_link.candidate_context: Bremen layover before the 2 February Saale departure
itinerary_link.archive_anchor: Bremen letter of 1 February 1892: Rudolf says he stayed at the Central Hotel opposite the station, called on the shipping agents Ehrhorn, Emden & Mayer next door, and remained in Bremen until the next morning's special train to Bremerhaven.
itinerary_link.reason: The note is wholly Bremen-specific and its internal order is spatially coherent with an urban errand sequence during the documented layover. No independent date is written on p26.

page_26.interpretive_limit: Do not claim procurement of metalware, jewelry, tools, or travel goods. The businesses are identifiable, but Rudolf's purpose at each address is presently unknown.

page_27.diplomatic_reading: Von New York bis Bremen sind 880 geographische Meilen
page_27.interpretation: Rudolf was converting or simplifying a source distance of 3520 into 880 'geographische Meilen' by an explicit 4:1 rule. The notebook therefore records travel arithmetic, not merely a copied place-name.
page_27.journey_relation: Strongly associated with the New York-Bremen Atlantic route and probably the return journey; the page itself is undated.
page_27.guard: Do not force the 880 figure into one standardized modern geographical-mile value. Rudolf's own arithmetic, source unit for 3520, and contemporary route convention have not yet been identified.

page_28.relationship: 27.5 cm is approximately 10.83 English inches, close to Rudolf's rounded 11-inch note.
page_28.interpretation: Practical metric-English dimensional conversion for a cylinder or cylindrical object. This extends the notebook's function from landscape observation and route calculation into measurement/translation between unit systems.
page_28.guard: The measured cylinder/object is unidentified. Do not connect it to a microscope, specimen jar, shipping cylinder, model component, or other apparatus without a separate source.

pdf_duplicate.finding: The two PDF pages embed byte-identical JPEG images despite separate PDF object references.
pdf_duplicate.interpretation: p13 is not independent evidence and the PDF is not a transparent one-frame-per-unique-leaf sequence.

older_backend_control.finding: The final 30 records of the older 700-frame Rakow OCR batch align with the current 30-page sketchbook PDF. Old records 682 and 683 contain the same extracted image filename (img_in_image_box_0_1_1315_801.jpg), matching the current p12/p13 duplication.
older_backend_control.interpretation: The duplicate predates the user's current PDF download and belongs to an earlier Corning/Rakow digital-delivery or processing chain. It is not a corruption introduced by the current local file.

digital_surrogate_integrity.catalogue_tempe_implication: Because the surrogate demonstrably contains a duplicated frame and the catalogue says the beginning sketch is Tempe, 22 April 1892 while the current PDF exposes Maricopa, 24 April as its first legible landscape caption, omission/reassembly in digital delivery remains a live explanation. Do not downgrade the catalogue to error without checking the individual JPG representation.

digital_delivery_target.known_public_delivery: Primo full display reports two digital representations: one PDF and 30 JPGs.
digital_delivery_target.technical_control: Ex Libris Alma Digital documentation states that digital delivery can be addressed by MMS ID or representation ID and exposes IIIF presentation manifests and per-file binary delivery once the representation identifier is known.
digital_delivery_target.next_step: Capture the actual 'Zoomable view' URL from Primo, extract its representation ID, request the corresponding IIIF manifest/file list, and compare all 30 JPG file identities/order with the PDF and old OCR batch. Priority question: does any delivered JPG contain the catalogued Tempe 22 April sketch?

functional_reassessment.knowledge_history_significance: The same portable object held visual, logistical, geographical and metrological work. It therefore documents the practical infrastructure of Rudolf's mobile knowledge production, not only its pictorial output.
